title: the measure of the killed run waits for the state of the run to settle
intent: The second half of wave F.  The check that proves the gate restarts a run that was killed read the state of the run -- the file of the attempts and the file of the map -- at the moment the gate had answered, and it read the words of the gate from the buffer that the filter of the process fills.  The writer of that state is the run, and the reader of it is the check, and the two are not one process: a reader that judges the state before the writer has finished it judges a state that is not there yet.  The red mark of the first gate of the package of the waves D3, D4, E1, E2 and E3 was exactly that refusal -- 'the map of the run was not written: the file ... is not there' (docs/PLAN.md §16.115) -- and the second red mark was the same shape in the sibling check (§16.116).  The measure now waits for the state to settle: the file of the attempts shows the restart, the file of the map holds the marker of the end of the run, and the output of the gate stops growing.  The wait is bounded (5 s for the state, 5 s for the words, 0.2 s of quiet), and a state that does not settle is a refusal with the same subject as before and not a comment.  The refusal now also names the words of the gate, so that a refusal about the map says what the gate said about the map.
objection: The cause of the flake of the wave 59 is not established here and is not named: no version of the cause is asserted in this wave.  What the wave removes is the class 'the measure judges a state before the writer of it has finished it' -- and the class is not the cause.  In the context of the check itself the race of the pipe did not appear in 20 runs of the instrumented copy (the buffer held the same 170 characters before and after the wait in every run); it appeared in a separate probe in 2 runs of 50, where a process that writes 4000 lines and dies leaves the buffer incomplete at the moment of its death.  The window is narrow, and that is measured, not inferred.  The promise itself did not change: the claim 'a-gate-run-needs-no-watchdog' and its registered control are the ones they were, and only the measure changed.
refuted_by: the run that was killed is not started again by the gate, or the map of the project is not written when the run ends, or a process of the run is still alive when the gate answered, or the gate holds a command that sleeps, or the wrapper of the project keeps a gate of its own
note: Measurements (all the mutations were made on copies of the tree in /tmp; the repository was not mutated).  Honest tree: 20 sequential runs, all exit 0, min 6806 ms, max 7182 ms, mean 6885 ms; 5 concurrent runs, all exit 0, min 7496 ms, max 7589 ms.  The same run on the check of the base takes 6640-6700 ms (mean 6653 ms): the added wait costs about 230 ms on the honest tree, and the wait for the state costs 0.00 ms there -- the state has already settled by the moment it is read.  Registered control of the claim (sed on scripts/gate: the increment of the attempt is replaced by 'verdict=3; break'), applied verbatim to a copy: exit 1 in 8688 ms, not 255 and no hang, and the refusal names its own subject -- 'gate: the killed run was not started again: the run was started 1 time(s), the second start is the restart (the state of the run did not settle in 5.0 seconds)'.  The wait does not turn the check into a comment: the mutation that takes the map step of the gate away gives exit 1 in 11932 ms -- 5047 ms more than the honest run, which is the limit of the wait, and the refusal says so -- with the same subject as before, 'the map of the run was not written: the file ... is not there; the state of the run did not settle in 5.0 seconds'.  The refusal names the words of the gate: the mutation that makes the map step of the gate fail (exit 3) gives 'the map of the run was not written: ...; the gate said: scripts/gate: the step map answered 3: the map of the project is not green; the state of the run did not settle in 5.0 seconds', and the diagnostic prints the whole output of the gate (three lines).  The word of the gate is looked for in the message of the line (after the first ': ') and not in the name of the program: the path of a copy of the tree holds the letters of 'map' and says nothing about the map (measured: without that rule the refusal caught the line '.../live-pilot: line 181: ... Killed').  The writer ran the check of the wave and nothing else: the `checks` list of this wave names three commands, and the two that the writer did not run (`./scripts/dev byte-compile-all` and `./scripts/dev check tests/checks/*`) are covered by the gate of the parent -- the gate of the wave F of 2026-11-22 (log /tmp/w-f-gate.log): 182 marks, not one of them of the first form, and both claims of the wave a pass with their negative control proven.  The numbers of the parent for the same scenarios are in docs/PLAN.md §16.118, and the table there names which number belongs to whom.  **The parent amended the measure of this wave on 2026-11-22 (commit 0c8a08c)**: the refusal always said that the state of the run did not settle, even when it had settled in 0.0 seconds, and a refusal with a false subject is worse than no subject at all; the measure now carries the state it measured (`yeah-gate--settle-note`).  The promise of the claim did not change.  Measured on the merged tree after the amendment: the honest tree answers 0 in 6955 ms; the scenario 'three starts' refuses with 'the state of the run settled in 0.0 seconds' (code 1); the scenario 'the gate writes no map' refuses with the former subject 'the state of the run did not settle in 5.0 seconds' (code 1, 12023 ms).  **The parent amended the measure of this wave again on 2026-11-22 (commit c672997)**: the re-gate of the wave (unit yeah-gate-f2, 19:24:38-19:43:56 UTC, log /tmp/w-f2-gate.log) gave one red mark on the claim of this wave -- 'the gate did not answer (pid 6359)' -- and the measure was repaired, not the promise: the gate is measured by the object of the process (the gate is a child of the check and Emacs knows its own child, and the object says the child is gone without a race), the wait answers the answer it found and asks its question at least once (a wait of no time is one question), and the code of the gate is read only after the gate has gone -- the code of a live process is 0, so the old assertion 'the gate answered 0' could not fail: it was a comment.  The cause of the red mark is not established and is not named: the check took about 7 seconds while the limit of its wait was 60 seconds, so the wait did not run out of time and the refusal came from a reading nobody asked for; the letter of the state of the gate was never anything but S and R in 3257 samples over its life; the number of a dead process stays free on this host and was still not taken after 60 seconds under a load that forks thousands of processes a second; and 240 runs of the instrumented copy plus another 240 under that load reproduced the race never.  Measured after the repair: the honest tree answers 0 in 6951 ms, the control 'the gate answers 1' refuses with 'the gate answered 1' (code 1), and the control 'the gate does not answer' refuses with 'the gate did not answer (pid 3023)' (code 1, 100515 ms -- exactly the limit of the wait).  The first version of the repair broke the path of the wait without time -- it asked nothing, and every number of the run read as alive -- and the honest run caught it.  The details are in `docs/PLAN.md` \u00a716.119.
